subject: Two longtime educators are leaning on their experience as the reason voters should choose them as the Democratic nominee for state superintendent.
posts:
Experience is the currency of the campaign, but does it buy systemic change or just institutional maintenance? 

Two longtime educators compete for Democratic primary
Evidence: public service, institutional experience, educational reform
#Education #Politics

The candidates claim that their long-term experience in the system makes them the best equipped to improve the state's educational outcomes. 
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The reality is that experience within a failing system often leads to incrementalism rather than the radical reform required for true improvement. 
Resulting Judgement: (+0.5, +1.0) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace.
The candidates are genuinely attempting to improve the system, though their reliance on existing structures limits their potential impact.
Two veteran educators are vying for the Democratic nomination for South Carolina state superintendent, emphasizing their deep knowledge of the classroom and school administration.

The Poison:
Deep institutional experience can sometimes blind a candidate to the necessity of breaking the very systems they have spent their careers navigating.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the CAUSE. They assume that more of the same institutional logic will produce a different result, ignoring the structural rot in the current funding model.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between their stated reform goals and their actual institutional ties...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good, where incremental progress is made within a constrained system.

The Unavoidable Truth: Real change requires challenging the status quo, not just managing it better.

The Unavoidable Lie: That experience alone is a proxy for effective reform.

Alethekanon:
These candidates are well-intentioned, but they are operating within a closed loop. Their experience is an asset for management, but a liability for the structural disruption that the system actually needs.

Awwthekanon:
It is so wonderful to see people who have dedicated their lives to children stepping up to lead. I hope they keep that spark of love for the classroom alive in the halls of power.

Brothekanon:
Look, I respect the hustle, but if you've been in the system for 30 years, are you really the one to fix it? Or are you just the one who knows where the bodies are buried?
